chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to us from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, who reported from Ubaid ibn Hamdoon al-Rawasi, who reported from al-Hasan Ibn Zareef, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, saying:
"Whenever I came across any judgement given by Ali, I always found it based on the principle of the (Prophet's) tradition."

He said: And Ali, peace be upon him, used to say: "If two disputants brought a case to me and I gave my judgement, and then if they came with the same case to me after many years, I would give the same judgement, because judgement never changes nor does it disappear, ever."

key_terms.أصل: basis, principle — the foundational root or evidence for a ruling
key_terms.السنة: the Sunnah — the established practice and precedent of the Prophet
key_terms.القضاء: judgement, judicial ruling — the authoritative resolution of a legal dispute

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq say about the consistency of Imam Ali's judicial rulings?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq testifies that every judicial ruling of Imam Ali was grounded in the Prophetic Sunnah. Ali himself affirmed the immutability of just judgement, stating he would rule identically on the same case regardless of how much time had passed. This hadith establishes Ali's unparalleled judicial authority and the principle that true justice, rooted in divine law, is timeless and unchanging.
